content:
Yesterday during the first Meta Cafe, I mentioned to @Thomas Murrills that I'd like to help with better formatting the reporting at #mathlib4 > Weekly linting log. As this has grown, it now has a couple of issues that make it less actionable: Zulip truncates the large message, it is not organized by the originating linter, and finding the corresponding source is awkward.

What I think would be ideal is if this is reorganized to be sorted by the linters in the weekly linting set, and the Zulip message lists counts and links to the corresponding part of the CI log for each linter to avoid truncation issues. This makes it easier to see what each linter is reporting and easier for those interested in helping with a particular linter to know where to look.

I can think of ways to hack this together, but the right way seems to be each tactic analysis linter produces a MessageData tagged with its name. We'd like the CI to enable the weekly set via lakefile option, build and somehow collect this MessageData, then do the sorting/reporting we want. The "somehow" is the part that remains mysterious to me. From #general > automatically apply code actions my understanding seems to be that Skimmer can aggregate this sort of data from a build, but looking at the lakefile facet this uses it remains a bit opaque to me. I'm also not sure of adjustments to the linter reporting, i.e. how might we need to adjust the current warnings and suggestions so that Skimmer can collect them tagged with the linter name?

(I'm a meta-code noob, but maybe this is helpful:)
FWIW I have made linters that log JSON (logInfo m!"{myJson.compress}"), and then collected those from the build log with a trivial grep + json.loads script.
Another idea is to change these logInfos into something that appends their message to an array in the env, and then add a final lean file that does import Mathlib and then dumps the entire array to a file.
If changing the linter code is off the table, maybe some fancy monad magic can capture these logInfo calls before they're printed to the screen, and tally them instead.

Snir Broshi said:

FWIW I have made linters that log JSON (logInfo m!"{myJson.compress}"), and then collected those from the build log with a trivial grep + json.loads script.

This is what I had in mind by "hack this together", but I was hoping to learn some more metaprogramming myself and possibly get something more maintainable as a result.

Snir Broshi said:

Another idea is to change these logInfos into something that appends their message to an array in the env, and then add a final lean file that does import Mathlib and then dumps the entire array to a file.

This could work too. Performance also isn't as important in this context.

Another consideration is we might like that the tactic analysis linters are still able to output human readable warnings/suggestions. While by design they will usually not be turned on by default, they can still be useful to enable during development.
Yeah but we can add a toggle between human readable and machine readable output

Re: how we might need to adjust the current warnings, if we went with a tagged MessageData approach: I think we’d want to adjust the underlying tactic analysis infrastructure to apply the tags automatically to every linter! That way individual tactic analysis linters don’t have to individually manage this.

Re: using skimmer: Yeah, at this point I’d (or we’d!) need to essentially provide a new lake facet + exe. (The goal is for it to be extensible in The Future.) But it’s pretty similar to the existing try-this one in some ways, and in some ways easier; I’d be happy to chat at some point and walk through it :)
Re: modifying the environment: this would be a good idea! However, linters are run underneath withoutModifyingEnv. This makes it impossible for them to persist anything into the environment. :(
If it is for "autonomous linting", then IO.Refs can be used by linters to persist information.
I really wish that there was an option for linters that would toggle the "withoutModifyingEnv" on and off.

Thomas Murrills said:

Re: using skimmer: Yeah, at this point I’d (or we’d!) need to essentially provide a new lake facet + exe. (The goal is for it to be extensible in The Future.) But it’s pretty similar to the existing try-this one in some ways, and in some ways easier; I’d be happy to chat at some point and walk through it :)

Sure, I'm interested in learning how to write facets for Skimmer, and thought maybe since you did a closely related one for tryThis already it could be a good reference point. Maybe I'll poke around some more a bit on my own first and we can discuss at some point, as I figure I'll get stuck :)

(And for the shorter term, Damiano's suggestion of IO.Ref remains available if The Future:tm: seems like something we should wait for)

Thanks everyone for the suggestions!

Picking up on @Thomas Murrills's suggestion that the tactic analysis framework should apply the tags, I took a stab at it and have a couple PRs up:

  • #43397 makes ContextInfo.runTacticCode drop any log messages the re-run tactic emits, so a pass only reports its own findings. (Without this, a pass that re-runs simp_all? would get the Try this hints incorrectly attributed to it.)
  • A follow-up, #43399, wraps each pass so every message it logs gets the same shape as Lean.Linter.logLint: the pass's option name as the message kind, the linter tag, and the usual can be disabled with note.

Something I only noticed while doing this: v4.34 added a persistent lint log (Lean.Linter.recordLints) that looks for this kind of data. After a build, the tagged messages are in the .olean (!). This means that lake lint --code-quality can print per-module, per-linter counts as JSON. That might be a reasonable input for a reorganized weekly report, and it may sidestep the "somehow collect the MessageData" question for now. It also keeps the door open to a Skimmer facet later.

Caveats: the PRs don't touch the weekly report. That would be a change to zulip_build_report.sh in mathlib-ci. I'm happy to look at those next if this direction seems right. I also noticed that lake lint --lint-only=linter.weeklyLintSet reported nothing for me, while --linters=linter.weeklyLintSet worked, so either I'm holding it wrong or set expansion in --lint-only needs a look. Not sure if this is a bug or I've got the wrong expectations.

Very much open to feedback. I think tagging after the fact is reasonable but perhaps this isn't the right approach. Another consideration is whether we want the disable note to be emitted from passes that are opt-in anyway.

I've done a bit more work on this and massaged the existing shell script into a Python script that properly groups linters. I'd love any feedback you may have! This goes hand-in-hand with the (still-open) Mathlib CI PR to tweak the the the TacticAnalyzer deals with logs and linters.
Is there a git mishap on mathlib-ci#70? The diff is currently very large.

The diff includes a whole build log, with linters enabled. I wanted to have some way of specifying the behavior, but this is admittedly an extremely large thing to add. Perhaps I could trim it down to, say, a hundred lines or so.
I've trimmed down the log text fitures to just a few dozen lines. That's enough.

I very much am in support of better formatting for the weekly linters and am happy to see you working on this. To make this easier to review though, I would defer all the testing aspects to another PR to make the weekly linting changes easier to review. (I also was imagining a Lean exe processing an IO.Ref of lints rather than putting this logic all into parsing logs from Python, but I don't know how universal this preference is)

Sounds good! I was a bit uneasy including the tests, to be honest. I feel a tension between CI being generally small-ish, fast scripts that are easy to diagnose and fix in production, as opposed to a more traditional approach with extensive unit testing. I'll update the PR.
